_comment: FinOps Foundation KPI correlation catalog (Phase 1). Curated subset of https://www.finops.org/finops-kpis/ that the scan output can inform. Each entry maps one or more source tools to a KPI. 'compute' = the server can calculate a value; 'informational' = the scan relates to the KPI but the value needs the field below or external input. Keep this honest: never claim a value we cannot derive.

domains.name: Understand usage and cost
domains.summary: Data acquisition, reporting, analysis, and alerting on top of your cost, usage, and carbon consumption.
domains.detail: This domain is about observability and business intelligence. It brings the data that stakeholders need together (ingestion) into a meaningful breakdown for the organization (allocation). That data can then be reported on (reporting) and monitored to proactively identify and react to issues (anomalies).
domains.capabilities: Data ingestion, Allocation, Reporting and analytics, Anomaly management

domains.name: Quantify business value
domains.summary: Identifying and breaking down cost, usage, and carbon emissions to stay aligned with organizational plans and measure the return on investment from cloud computing efforts.
domains.detail: This domain is about measuring and maximizing the business value each team and workload gets from the cloud to maximize future potential.
domains.capabilities: Planning and estimating, Forecasting, Budgeting, Benchmarking, Unit economics

domains.name: Optimize usage and cost
domains.summary: Designing and optimizing solutions for efficiency to ensure you get the most out of your cloud investments.
domains.detail: Rate optimization lowers the price paid for resources already in use, through commitment discounts and licensing benefits. Usage optimization reduces what is consumed, by removing waste and rightsizing what remains.
domains.capabilities: Architecting for the cloud, Usage optimization, Rate optimization, Licensing and SaaS, Cloud sustainability

domains.name: Manage the FinOps practice
domains.summary: Establishing a clear and consistent vision of FinOps and driving cultural adoption across your organization.
domains.detail: Unlike domains that focus on FinOps tasks to drive efficiency and maximize value, this domain emphasizes managing and supporting your FinOps practice.
domains.capabilities: FinOps education and enablement, FinOps practice operations, Onboarding workloads, Governance, policy, and risk, Invoicing and chargeback, FinOps assessment, FinOps tools and services, Intersecting frameworks

kpis.name: Cost per Gigabyte Stored
kpis.definition: Month-to-date amortized storage cost divided by current reported managed-disk and storage-account capacity.
kpis.calculation: StorageCost / TotalStorageGb for the captured cost period.
requiredInputs: Amortized storage cost and billing currency
kpis.interpretation: Compare like-for-like storage tiers, redundancy, access patterns, and periods against your own workload baseline. No universal healthy rate applies.
kpis.limitations: A blended cost divided by current capacity, not GB-hours. Provisioned disks and used storage-account capacity are different measures. Partial capacity measurements can distort the rate; this is not a quoted storage price. A returned zero, especially early in the period, can reflect billing-data delay rather than free capacity.
kpis.plainLanguage: Month-to-date amortized storage cost per GB of reported current capacity.
kpis.exploreHint: Run the Storage Tier Advice scan to see if moving cold data to Cool or Archive lowers this.

kpis.name: Hourly Cost per CPU Core
kpis.definition: Average cost per CPU core, giving unit-cost insight for compute.
kpis.calculation: ComputeCost / TotalVCpu / elapsed hours in the captured UTC cost period, with a minimum one-hour divisor.
requiredInputs: Amortized VM compute cost and billing currency
Captured UTC cost-period start and end
kpis.interpretation: Compare equivalent VM families, regions, licensing, discounts, and operating schedules. Use workload-specific baselines, not a universal price target.
kpis.limitations: Current inventory includes stopped VMs and is not time-weighted running vCPU-hours. Newly added or removed VMs can distort the average. Historical results without captured dates use the current UTC month window. A returned zero can reflect billing-data delay, especially early in the period.
kpis.plainLanguage: Period spend spread across current vCPU inventory and elapsed calendar hours, not measured running-core hours.
kpis.exploreHint: Run the Optimization Advice or Idle VMs scan to find rightsizing that lowers this.

kpis.name: Effective Average Compute Cost per Core
kpis.definition: Month-to-date amortized VM compute cost divided by current vCPU inventory.
kpis.calculation: ComputeCost / TotalVCpu for the captured cost period.
requiredInputs: Amortized VM compute cost and billing currency
kpis.interpretation: Compare the same elapsed period and a comparable fleet. A lower amount alone does not establish improved efficiency.
kpis.limitations: Not a full-month forecast. Current inventory includes stopped VMs; SKU lookup failures can approximate capacity. Only the VM compute meter categories selected by this scan are included. A returned zero can reflect billing-data delay and does not prove that compute is free.
kpis.plainLanguage: Month-to-date compute spend per currently provisioned vCPU, including stopped VMs in the inventory.
kpis.exploreHint: Pair with utilization, SKU, runtime, and commitment evidence before changing the fleet.

kpis.name: Percentage of Costs Associated with Untagged Resources
kpis.definition: Percentage of cloud cost on resources missing a required tag, per your tagging policy.
kpis.calculation: 100 x UnallocatedCost / ResourceCostSeen. Legacy results fall back to the highest untagged cost share among recognized allocation tags.
requiredInputs: Complete cost coverage in one currency
Cost with no recognized allocation tag; or comparable per-tag cost rows
kpis.interpretation: Lower is generally better for allocation. Set an organizational target and agreed exceptions; this does not measure all missing tags.
kpis.limitations: Recognized allocation-tag presence is a proxy, not validation of required tag values or ownership. Non-resource charges are outside this denominator. Credits and nonpositive totals can prevent calculation.
kpis.plainLanguage: How much of your spend lands on resources that are not tagged.
kpis.exploreHint: Run the Tag Recommendations scan to see which CAF tags to backfill and where.

kpis.name: Percentage of Costs Associated with Unallocated Resources
kpis.definition: Percentage of spend that cannot be attributed to a team, project, or application.
kpis.calculation: 100 x UnallocatedCost / ResourceCostSeen, using recognized allocation-tag presence as the allocation proxy.
requiredInputs: Complete resource-cost coverage in one currency
UnallocatedCost or comparable per-tag cost rows
kpis.interpretation: Aim to reduce unexplained resource spend against your allocation policy. A tagged resource still needs a valid, agreed owner.
kpis.limitations: Not verified chargeback completeness. Shared and non-resource charges need separate allocation. Legacy per-tag results use the worst recognized allocation tag rather than a sum across tags.
kpis.plainLanguage: Share of your bill you cannot yet assign to an owner.
kpis.exploreHint: Backfill allocation tags (Customer/project/CostCenter), then re-run the Cost by Tag scan.

kpis.name: Percentage of Costs that are Tagging Policy Compliant
kpis.definition: Allocation-tag presence proxy: the share of resource cost carrying a recognized allocation tag, not verified organizational policy compliance.
kpis.calculation: 100 minus the resource-cost share with no recognized allocation tag; legacy results use the worst recognized allocation tag.
requiredInputs: Complete cost coverage in one currency
kpis.interpretation: Higher indicates better allocation-tag presence. It is not proof of compliance with your required tags, allowed values, or Azure Policy.
kpis.limitations: This proxy does not validate tag values, all required tags, ownership, or non-resource charges. Missing or incomplete cost coverage remains unavailable.
kpis.plainLanguage: Share of resource spend carrying a recognized allocation tag, not verified policy compliance.
kpis.exploreHint: Run the Policy Recommendations scan to deploy tag-enforcement policy.

kpis.name: Commitment Utilization Score
kpis.definition: Burndown of pre-purchased commitment capacity against actual consumption. ~100% is healthy; lower signals shelfware.
kpis.calculation: Mean of the available RIAvgUtilization and SPAvgUtilization values, including only families with a positive commitment count.
requiredInputs: Measured family-average utilization over their reported windows
kpis.interpretation: Values closer to 100% indicate less unused purchased capacity. Review individual commitments before renewal or purchase decisions.
kpis.limitations: A simple average of family averages, not a spend-weighted portfolio utilization. It is distinct from commitment coverage of eligible spend. The source windows can differ.
kpis.plainLanguage: How much of your reserved/committed capacity you are actually using.
kpis.exploreHint: Run the Reservation Advice scan to right-size future commitments.

kpis.name: Percentage of Commitment Discount Waste
kpis.definition: Percentage of commitment capacity not applied to on-demand spend (wasted).
kpis.calculation: 100 minus the mean of available reservation and savings-plan family utilization averages.
kpis.interpretation: Lower suggests less unused purchased capacity. Confirm the affected commitments and their cost before estimating a monetary loss.
kpis.limitations: An unweighted utilization proxy, not measured wasted currency or proof of business waste. Absent commitment families are excluded rather than treated as zero utilization.
kpis.plainLanguage: The slice of your reservations/savings plans you paid for but did not use.
kpis.exploreHint: 100% minus your utilization. Investigate underused commitments for renewal changes.

kpis.name: Percent of Compute Spend Covered by Commitment Discounts
kpis.definition: Percentage of compute cost (excluding Spot) covered by commitment discounts.
kpis.calculation: 100 x CommittedAmortized / (CommittedAmortized + OnDemandAmortized), as returned by the savings scan.
requiredInputs: Eligible amortized usage charges by pricing model
kpis.interpretation: Set coverage targets around predictable demand and acceptable commitment risk. Higher coverage is not automatically better for variable demand.
kpis.limitations: Excludes Spot, purchases, refunds, and unused commitment charges from the eligible basis. This is not commitment utilization or a savings percentage.
kpis.plainLanguage: How much of your eligible spend rides on a discounted commitment (reservation or savings plan) versus full on-demand. Computed from amortized cost by pricing model, excluding Spot from the eligible base.
kpis.exploreHint: Raise coverage by buying reservations or savings plans for steady-state workloads.

kpis.name: Percent of Unused Resources
kpis.definition: The count of orphan candidates returned by the scan, rather than a measured percentage of unused resources or spend.
kpis.calculation: TotalCount of resources flagged by the orphaned-resource scan; a percentage is not calculated.
kpis.interpretation: Review the candidates for legitimate dependencies, recovery purposes, ownership, and cost. There is no universal acceptable count.
kpis.limitations: A candidate count, not confirmed business waste or a share of spend. Counts across resource types have different financial impacts.
kpis.plainLanguage: Number of orphan candidates returned, not a measured percentage of unused resources.
kpis.exploreHint: Confirm nothing depends on them, then delete them in the Azure portal or with Azure CLI.

kpis.name: Computational Waste Percentage
kpis.definition: Scan proxy: the percentage of currently running VMs flagged idle or underutilized, not a percentage of wasted spend.
kpis.calculation: 100 x idle-or-underutilized candidate count / currently running VMs scanned. Missing metrics suppress the percentage.
kpis.interpretation: Lower means fewer VMs meet this scan's screening rules. Review the Calculation and thresholds section; no candidates is not proof of optimized compute.
kpis.limitations: Count-weighted, not cost-weighted. Does not assess memory, disk activity, peaks, availability, or business utility. Averages can hide bursts.
kpis.plainLanguage: Compute you are running and paying for but barely using. Shown as the share of running VMs flagged idle or underutilized.
kpis.exploreHint: Deallocate confirmed idle VMs in the Azure portal or with Azure CLI. Deallocating is reversible; the disks keep billing.

kpis.name: Percent Storage on Frequent Access Tier
kpis.definition: Percentage of object storage held on a frequent (Hot) access tier.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: 100 x Hot-tier blob bytes / all in-scope blob bytes. This scan does not calculate it.
requiredInputs: Per-blob tier and byte inventory across all relevant tiers
kpis.interpretation: There is no target Hot-tier percentage. Select tiers according to access patterns, latency, retention, and total cost.
kpis.limitations: The scan selects accounts with Hot or unspecified default tier. That default does not establish each blob's tier or the byte-weighted distribution.
kpis.plainLanguage: How much of your storage sits on the most expensive Hot tier.
kpis.exploreHint: Flagged Hot accounts with low activity are candidates for Cool or Archive.

kpis.name: Storage Decay Ratio
kpis.definition: Storage cost attributed to data not accessed within a set window (dark data).
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: 100 x storage cost for data not accessed within an agreed window / comparable storage cost. Not calculated here.
requiredInputs: Per-blob access history and retention window
kpis.interpretation: Unused-looking data may have recovery or compliance value. Assess net savings and retrieval requirements before changing retention or tier.
kpis.limitations: Account-level transaction counts cannot identify individual cold blobs or their cost. Low activity is a screening signal, not a measured decay ratio.
kpis.plainLanguage: Share of storage spend on data nobody has touched recently.
kpis.exploreHint: Low-activity accounts in this scan approximate dark data; apply lifecycle policy.

kpis.name: CSP Cloud Budget Burn Rate
kpis.definition: Average percentage consumed across comparable budgets, not a time-normalized burn rate.
kpis.calculation: Mean of 100 x ActualSpend / Amount across budgets with verified comparable monthly windows and currencies.
requiredInputs: One currency and comparable current-month periods
kpis.interpretation: Compare with the expected spending profile for the elapsed budget period. This is percent consumed, not a time-normalized spending velocity.
kpis.limitations: Unweighted across budgets. Multiple budgets within one subscription, missing fields, or incompatible periods make the aggregate unavailable. Forecast availability is separate.
kpis.plainLanguage: How fast you are spending against your budget this period. Shown as the average percent of budget consumed across all budgets.
kpis.exploreHint: Risk levels in the scan flag budgets trending over. Adjust thresholds or spend.

kpis.name: Percentage Variance of Budgeted vs. Actual Spend
kpis.definition: Actual spend as a percentage of comparable budget amounts; the displayed value is percent of plan, not signed variance.
kpis.calculation: The displayed value is 100 x total actual spend / total budget amount, expressed as percent of plan, not signed variance.
requiredInputs: Common currency and verified reporting window
kpis.interpretation: Compare period-to-date consumption with the spending plan and available forecasts. A value below 100% does not by itself establish that spending is on track.
kpis.limitations: Overlapping budgets are not combined. The displayed ratio is not forecast accuracy, and a missing forecast is not zero.
kpis.plainLanguage: How far your actual spend is from what you planned. Shown as total actual vs total budgeted across all budgets.
kpis.exploreHint: Compare budget amount vs actual in the scan rows.

kpis.name: Anomaly Detection Rate
kpis.definition: Observed anomaly-alert and configured-rule counts, not a measured detection rate or avoided cost.
kpis.calculation: Observed anomaly-alert count and configured anomaly-rule count. No detection-rate denominator is available.
kpis.interpretation: Confirm useful alert coverage and response ownership. More alerts are not necessarily better, and no alerts does not prove that no anomalies occurred.
kpis.limitations: A count proxy, not detection recall, avoided cost, or a rate over all actual anomalies. Inventory failures leave it unavailable.
kpis.plainLanguage: How often unusual cost spikes are being caught. Shown as a proxy: anomaly alerts triggered plus the number of detection rules configured (a true rate needs the count of anomalies that occurred, which Azure does not expose).
kpis.exploreHint: Configure anomaly alert rules so spikes are caught proactively.

kpis.name: Estimated commitment savings
kpis.definition: A month-to-date commitment savings estimate for usage charges in the reported billing currency, using assumed discounts rather than measured savings.
kpis.calculation: RISavingsMonthToDate + SPSavingsMonthToDate from the scanner's assumed-discount model. AHB is reported separately.
requiredInputs: Known single currency and captured UTC period
kpis.interpretation: Use only as a review estimate. Establish realized savings using matched pay-as-you-go counterfactuals and benefit charges.
kpis.limitations: Assumes 40% RI and 25% savings-plan discounts; excludes purchases, refunds, unused commitment charges, and the separate AHB estimate. Not annualized and not a measured effective savings rate.
kpis.plainLanguage: This scan estimates commitment savings for the reported UTC period, not a savings percentage or an annual projection. Azure Hybrid Benefit has a separate USD estimate for 730 hours and isn't added to this amount. Actual discounts vary by SKU, term, region, and agreement.
kpis.exploreHint: Validate the estimate against matching pay-as-you-go rates and benefit usage before reporting realized savings.

kpis.name: Percentage of Legacy Resource
kpis.definition: Percentage of resources running on older generation types vs modern equivalents.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: 100 x legacy resources / comparable resource inventory. Only candidate counts are returned by this scan.
kpis.interpretation: Prioritize by support deadlines, workload risk, migration effort, and verified price-performance rather than targeting an arbitrary percentage.
kpis.limitations: Different resource types are not financially equivalent. A newer SKU does not by itself prove a cost saving.
kpis.plainLanguage: How much of your estate runs on older, less efficient resource types.
kpis.exploreHint: Modernizing to newer SKUs usually improves price-performance.

kpis.name: Carbon per Unit of Cloud Spend
kpis.definition: Carbon emissions (CO2e) per unit of cloud spend, ideally drillable by service category.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: emissions / spend for the same scope and reporting period. Not calculated here.
requiredInputs: Matching reporting month and subscription scope
kpis.interpretation: Compare the same workload and methodology over time. Pair with useful output measures; currency changes or prices alone can change the ratio.
kpis.limitations: Published carbon data can lag cost data. Current-month spend cannot be substituted for an older carbon-reporting month.
kpis.plainLanguage: Carbon per unit of spend requires matching emissions and cost periods.
kpis.exploreHint: Carbon-efficient regions and modern SKUs reduce this.

kpis.name: Token Consumption Metrics
kpis.definition: Cost of token-based models based on input/output token usage.
kpis.calculation: TotalTokens, with available TotalAICost shown separately for the reported period. This entry is not cost per token.
requiredInputs: Comparable cost and currency to show the spend figure
kpis.interpretation: Relate token demand to useful output, model choice, and input/output mix. Token volume alone is neither good nor bad.
kpis.limitations: Usage can be partial when metric reads fail. Total AI spend may include accounts without measured tokens; it is not an attributed cost of those tokens.
kpis.plainLanguage: How many tokens your AI workloads burn and what they cost.
kpis.exploreHint: Prompt engineering and model choice move this number.

kpis.name: Cost per API Call
kpis.definition: Average cost for each API call made to AI services.
kpis.calculation: CostPerRequest: costs of accounts with measured requests divided by their measured request count for the reported period.
requiredInputs: Complete metric coverage and no RateIssue
kpis.interpretation: Compare the same model, request mix, service quality, and period with your workload baseline. Cheap failed requests are not a business improvement.
kpis.limitations: Blended across measured accounts. Missing or mismatched measurements suppress the rate; it is not a per-model price quote or cost per successful business outcome.
kpis.plainLanguage: What each AI service request costs you on average.
kpis.exploreHint: High per-call cost can signal an inefficient model or call pattern.

kpis.name: Percentage of Unallocated Shared Cost
kpis.definition: Shared expenses that cannot be directly attributed to a specific team or project.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: 100 x unallocated shared cost / agreed shared-cost pool. Not calculated as a KPI here.
kpis.interpretation: Reduce unexplained shared cost under an agreed allocation policy. Arithmetic reconciliation alone does not establish fair allocation.
kpis.limitations: Allocation outputs are read-only showback proposals, not applied billing rules or proof of acceptance by workload owners.
kpis.plainLanguage: Shared platform cost not yet split across its consumers.
kpis.exploreHint: Split it with a shared cost allocation or usage-proportional allocation scan.

kpis.name: Allocation Accuracy Index (AAI)
kpis.definition: Percentage of total cost directly and accurately attributed to responsible owners.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: 100 x cost confirmed as correctly allocated / total comparable cost. Not calculated here.
kpis.interpretation: Set targets with finance and workload owners. Validate correctness separately from whether every cent was allocated.
kpis.limitations: Tag presence and allocations that sum to the pool cannot prove ownership accuracy. External validation is required.
kpis.plainLanguage: How reliably your costs map to the right team or project.
kpis.exploreHint: Improve tagging and shared-cost rules to raise this.

kpis.name: Total Cost of Ownership per Workload
kpis.definition: Average full-lifecycle cost of running an individual workload (compute, storage, network, etc.).
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: all agreed direct, shared, licensing, and operating costs attributable to a workload over its stated lifecycle or period. Not calculated here.
requiredInputs: Shared, licensing, and non-cloud operating costs
kpis.interpretation: Compare equivalent workload scope, service quality, and lifecycle assumptions, preferably per business outcome.
kpis.limitations: The VM cost breakdown is a partial resource-cost view, not full business TCO. External and shared costs need separate evidence.
kpis.plainLanguage: The true all-in cost of one workload, not just its compute line.
kpis.exploreHint: The VM cost breakdown scan decomposes a VM into all its billed meters.

kpis.name: Frequency of Data Updates
kpis.definition: Time between updates of cost data (e.g. since the last export refresh).
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: elapsed time between successful data refreshes. Not calculated in this report.
requiredInputs: At least two verified refresh timestamps for each source
kpis.interpretation: Compare actual update cadence with the agreed data-freshness objective.
kpis.limitations: A last-refresh timestamp alone establishes recency, not update frequency. Discovery results are not attached as KPI measurements by this launcher.
kpis.plainLanguage: How current the cost data behind your answers is.
kpis.exploreHint: The Freshness date in this tool is your data-update recency.

kpis.name: Cost Visibility Delay
kpis.definition: Time between a cost occurring and it being ingested, normalized, and visible.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: time a charge becomes queryable minus its usage or charge occurrence time. Not calculated in this report.
kpis.interpretation: Compare observed latency with the reporting objective for each source. Different services and agreements can have different delays.
kpis.limitations: Neither scan time nor a latest-export timestamp establishes end-to-end visibility delay. Live API data is not guaranteed to be real-time.
kpis.plainLanguage: The lag between spending money and seeing it in reports.
kpis.exploreHint: Compare charge and ingestion timestamps before making a data-latency claim.

kpis.name: Unified Cost & Usage Visibility
kpis.definition: Extent to which all relevant cost and usage sources are integrated into one reporting system.
kpis.calculation: Reference formula: 100 x validated covered units / agreed total in-scope units. Not calculated in this report.
requiredInputs: Agreed coverage basis, such as spend, subscriptions, or sources
kpis.interpretation: Declare the coverage basis and gaps. Subscription coverage and percentage of spend covered are not interchangeable.
kpis.limitations: A configured connection does not prove complete data delivery. This launcher does not attach source-discovery coverage as a measured KPI.
kpis.plainLanguage: How much of your estate is covered by one unified cost view.
kpis.exploreHint: CoveragePct in this tool reflects how much of scope the hub/export covers.
